'''Isaac Mathieu Weill''' (24 May 1851 – 5 November 1939) was a French [[mathematician]] and principal of the [[Lycée Chaptal|Collège Chaptal]].

==Biography==
Mathieu Weill was born to a [[Jews|Jewish]] family in [[Haguenau]], the son of Valentine and Isidore Weill, a mathematics teacher. He was educated in the [[lyceums]] of [[Bourg-en-Bresse|Burg]] and [[Strasbourg|Strasburg]], and was admitted to the [[École Polytechnique]] in 1870. He received a degree in mathematics in November 1872, and a degree in physical sciences in November 1876. {{r|brasseur}} Meanwhile, Weill began studies at the [[School of Applied Artillery|military school]] in [[Fontainebleau]] in 1872. He attained the rank of [[lieutenant]] of [[artillery]], but resigned in April 1877.

He married Delphine Lévi in 1878, with whom he had four children.{{r|brasseur}} That same year, he became a lecturer at the [[Lycée Chaptal|Collège Chaptal]] at Paris. He was appointed professor of mathematics in 1881, and in October 1898 the school's principal.{{r|JE}} He was appointed Chevalier of the [[Legion of Honour]] on 28 February 1904.<ref>{{Base Léonore|L2752003}}</ref>

==Publications==
Weill published several essays in French mathematical journals, including the ''[[Nouvelles Annales de Mathématiques]]'' and the ''[[Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de France]]''.{{r|brasseur}} He was the author of "Cours de Géométrie Analytique" (1888) and of "Précis d'Arithmétique, de Géométrie, d'Algèbre, de Trigonométrie," in four volumes (1895–1897).<ref>{{cite web|first=Jean|last=Daltroff|date=2002|title=Quelques figures méconnues du judaïsme alsacien: Les Weil et les Weill|website=Judaïsme d'Alsace et de Lorraine|url=http://judaisme.sdv.fr/perso/weills.htm|access-date=3 March 2019}}</ref>
